validated_results.title: Variation of urinary and serum trace elements (Ca, Zn, Cu, Se) in bladder carcinoma in China.
validated_results.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
validated_results.reason: Human case-control study comparing urinary and serum calcium between bladder carcinoma cases and healthy controls, reporting calcium levels as related to bladder carcinoma risk, though no separable risk estimate is given.

extraction.comparison_type: cases versus healthy controls (serum and urinary calcium levels)
extraction.population: Patients with bladder carcinoma and healthy persons in China

sample_size.excerpt: To determine this, 81 patients with bladder carcinoma chosen as a study group and 130 healthy persons chosen as a control group were all assayed for urinary and serum trace elements (calcium [Ca], zinc [Zn], copper [Cu], selenium [Se]) using an atomic absorption spectrophotometer, and the results were analyzed by independent sample t tests.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 81 + 130 = 211

cases.excerpt: Since there are few studies of the effect of trace elements in bladder carcinoma in China, the aim of this study was thus to assess variation using a case control approach. comparison.excerpt: The results showed urinary Ca, Zn and serum Cu levels of the study group to be significantly higher (P<0.05) than those of he control group.
